title: Theme variations are ignored when getting theme properties of a type other than the caller's class
body: ### Tested versions 4.7.dev [40448082abe972daa179c64d7889cd88a8e7ea9c]; also 4.4.1 ### System information Windows 11, Godot 4.7.dev, ### Issue description I got an issue with theme type variations, maybe it's due to a lack of understanding: When some parts of a Control node are drawn, theme items are obtained with no particular `theme_type`, in which case variations are applied normally. Sometimes however, a type is specified which does not match the class_name of the drawing node. As an example, I am working on a Godot plugin, and wanted to use the `EditorSpinSlider`, and I'd like to style its font color. The `EditorSpinSlider` which extends `Range` draws the value with a font color, that it obtains via `get_theme_color("font_color", "LineEdit")`. Since the `EditorSpinSlider` is not a `LineEdit`, it is not possible to provide a theme variation that affects the color of the label, regardless of whether the base type of the variation is Node, LineEdit or EditorSpinSlider. The label however, which gets its font color with a call to `get_theme_color("label_color")` can be styled using a variation. This affects a lot of editor nodes, but not exclusively. Another example would be the `"scroll_speed"` constant on a scroll container, or the `"save"`, `"load"` and `"clear"` icons in a color picker (shown when you open the three-dot menu on the swatches), which are obtained from within the ColorPicker class, but cannot be changed with a variation on it. I did notice that the icons can be changed, by e.g. adding an icon item `"save"` in the `FileDialog` type to the theme, but there is no way to style those using variations. Is this a bug, or what is the intention behind disallowing variations to affect certain parts of a node? I asked this in the contributor chat, but got no answer. In essence, in `theme_owners.cpp` -> `void ThemeOwner::get_theme_type_dependencies()`, why the restriction to `p_theme_type == type_variation`? ### Steps to reproduce Create a Theme and add it to a ColorPicker node. Add a Theme Variation `MyColorPicker`, with `ColorPicker` base, and add a `save` icon item. Run scene, click on the swatches three-dot, and observe that the `save` icon is ignored. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [theme-variation-issue.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25323748/theme-variation-issue.zip)
